The '''[[Talak (world)|Talak system]]''' has two inhabited planets, presumably both colonized by the same long-forgotten expedition.

== Description (Specifications) {{Unpublished cite|author= the Wiki editorial team: the system's published characteristics (provided in ''[[Uragyad'n of the Seven Pillars]]'') have been significantly updated, bringing the background data more in line with the current canon system data.}} ==
The system is centered on a solitary primary star named ''Nijet''.
{{MonostellarSystem
|name           = Talak
|primary        = G7 III 
|PrimaryName    = Nijet
|PrimaryNotes   = Unstable pulsating star. It occasionally experiences powerful [[Flare Star|flare activity]], causing [[Electromagnetic Spectrum|intense EM noise]].
}}

=== System Data ===
The worlds of the [[Talak (system)|system]] have been surveyed. They consist of:
* The [[mainworld]], Talak, orbiting at [[Astronomical Unit|10.8 AU]].
* x2 secondary [[world|rocky worlds]]. These are inhabited [[Vahjdi (world)|Vahjdi]], orbiting at [[Astronomical Unit|8.7 AU]], and [[corrosive atmosphere]] Monkodo, orbiting at [[Astronomical Unit|14.2 AU]].
* x1 [[Gas Giant|large gas giant]], Galsimar, orbiting at [[Astronomical Unit|18.7 AU]].
** It retains a number of [[Natural Satellite|large moons]].
* x1 [[planetoid belt]], the Kasama Belt, lying at a mean distance of [[Astronomical Unit|25.0 AU]].

== History & Background (Dossier) ==
[[File:Comp-Prog-Dav-R-Deitrick-Starter-Trav-Page-16 16-July-2018a.jpg|right]]
==== Talak ====
[[Talak (world)|Talak]], the second world out from the star and the [[mainworld]] of the system, has an orbital period of [[Year|18 years]] [[Day|335 days]] ([[Day|6,909 standard days]]).

==== Vahjdi ====
The innermost world, [[Vahjdi (world)|Vahjdi]], has an orbital period of [[Year|13 years]] [[Day|247 days]] ([[Day|4,995 standard days]]). It has a very slow rotation period: one local day is equivalent to [[Day|70 standard days]] ([[Hour|almost 1700 standard hours]]).
* There are 71.4 local days in a local year.
* During the local day, the world experiences around [[Hour|100 hours]] of dawn, [[Hour|750 hours]] of daylight, [[Hour|100 hours]] of twilight, and [[Hour|750 hours]] of night.

It retains a fairly close, [[Natural Satellite|relatively large moon]] that orbits once every [[Week|standard week]].
* Vahjdi experiences libration, a characteristic wobble with a frequency of [[Hour|33 hours]], caused by [[Natural Satellite|the moon]] and the [[mainworld]] orbiting their barycenter.
* This wobble causes the star to rise and fall in the sky during the long local day, giving brighter and darker periods.
